## GET /admin-api/xacml

`getXacml`

**The Policy Decision Point settings and current status**

The Settings tab on /admin/xacml, as JSON.

THIS IS THE ONLY FAMILY ON THIS SERVICE THAT ANSWERS A QUESTION ABOUT SOMEBODY ELSE'S BOUNDARY. Every other protocol here authenticates or provisions a person; this one is handed a subject who was authenticated somewhere else and asked whether they may.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-condition

`addXacmlCondition`

**Add a Condition to a rule**

A boolean expression evaluated AFTER the Target matches. **At most one per rule** — the schema allows exactly one, and the editor stops offering this on a rule that has one rather than offering it and then refusing, because an option that is offered and refused teaches a caller that the menu is not to be trusted.

It must evaluate to EXACTLY ONE BOOLEAN. A condition returning a bag, or an integer, is a static type error and the policy is refused at write time rather than going Indeterminate on every request.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-match

`addXacmlMatch`

**Add a Match to an alternative**

One attribute tested against one value. It arrives COMPLETE AND VALID — a function, a literal and a designator — because an editor that produced half-built elements would hold a document that cannot be saved, and a document that cannot be saved cannot be evaluated, which is when you most want to look at it. ## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-policy

`addXacmlPolicyToSet`

**Add a Policy inside a PolicySet**

A PolicySet holds POLICIES; a Policy holds RULES. They are not two spellings of one thing, and asking for a rule on a policy set is refused rather than written somewhere it will not be read.

The new policy arrives with `deny-unless-permit` and no rules, which decides Deny. That is deliberate: this editor is LIVE, so a child added to the running root takes effect on the next request, and one that began permissive would be a hole opened by pressing Add.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-policy-reference

`addXacmlPolicyReference`

**Reference a policy stored separately in the repository**

THIS IS HOW A PDP REACHES MORE THAN ONE DOCUMENT. Evaluation starts at the root policy and a `PolicyIdReference` is resolved against the repository WHEN A DECISION IS MADE, not when the document is loaded — so referencing a policy that has not been written yet is allowed and is not an error. An unresolved reference is reported on the decision instead, which is what keeps the order two policies are authored in from mattering.

The `ref` is the PolicyId INSIDE the other document, not its directory entry name.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-rule-obligation

`addXacmlRuleObligation`

**Add an obligation to a rule**

Fires when this RULE's Effect is the decision. An obligation is the half of a decision that says "yes, AND you must also do this", and section 7.2 makes it binding: a PEP that cannot discharge one MUST NOT grant the access. ## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-target-anyof

`addXacmlTargetClause`

**Add a Target clause to a policy, a rule or a Target**

A `<Target>` is a list of clauses and **every one of them must match** — they are ANDed. Inside a clause the alternatives are ORed and inside an alternative the Matches are ANDed again, so the quantifier flips at each of the three levels.

That is why the element names read backwards from what they do: `AnyOf` holds `AllOf` holds `Match`, and the `AnyOf`s themselves are ANDed. Getting it wrong produces a policy that applies to more or less than was meant and never an error.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-variable

`addXacmlVariable`

**Add a VariableDefinition to a policy**

Names an expression so several rules can share it — and so it is evaluated ONCE per request rather than once per use.

ITS SCOPE IS THE POLICY IT IS ON. A sibling policy in the same set cannot name it (section 5.24), which is why GET /admin-api/xacml/editor is the only reliable source of what a VariableReference at a given path may legally name.

It arrives holding a designator, because a VariableDefinition with no expression is a document that will not load. Replace it with any of the set-expression actions.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/authzen/approve-access-request

`approveAuthzenAccessRequest`

**Approve an AuthZEN access request**

Approves a pending access request (#1180) as the caller, after the access-control policy (action approve-access-request on resource authzen-access-request) permitted it — refused, among others, for the request's own subject. The approval is handed to the PEP, whose next evaluation the realm's policy decides afresh. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-authzen` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/authzen/set-attribute

`setAuthzenAttribute`

**Add or replace one row of the AuthZEN attribute catalogue**

Writes one authzenAttribute value on the realm's sts-authzen-api object, replacing the row for the same object and property. Refused for a row the catalogue's grammar refuses (STS-AUTHZEN-0010) and for one mapping onto a reserved identifier (STS-AUTHZEN-0011, 0012): a request-supplied attribute suppresses the PIP. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-authzen` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributeId` | string | yes | The XACML attribute it is sent as. Never urn:sts:xacml:*, subject-id, resource-id or action-id, nor a bare directory name in a subject category. |
| `category` | string |  | access-subject, resource, action, environment (or another XACML category, or its URI); the object's own when empty. |
| `dataType` | string |  | string, boolean, integer, double, date, dateTime, time, anyURI, dayTimeDuration, yearMonthDuration, hexBinary, base64Binary, rfc822Name, x500Name, dnsName, ipAddress, or the type's URI; string when empty. |
| `description` | string |  | Free text for administrators. |
| `multiplicity` | one of `single`, `bag` |  | single (one value) or bag (a JSON array); single when left out. |
| `object` | one of `subject`, `resource`, `action`, `context` | yes | The AuthZEN object the property is on. |
| `property` | string | yes | The property's name, or a dotted path into a nested object (owner.country). For context, the member's name; context.application is reserved. |

**200**: The row as stored.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changed` | boolean |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `removed` | string |  |  |
| `replaced` | boolean |  |  |
| `row` | object |  |  |
| `row.attributeId` | string |  |  |
| `row.category` | string |  |  |
| `row.dataType` | string |  |  |
| `row.description` | string |  |  |
| `row.key` | string |  |  |
| `row.multiplicity` | string |  |  |
| `row.object` | string |  |  |
| `row.property` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

|---|---|---|---|
| `changed` | boolean |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/create-from-template

`createXacmlPolicy`

**Create a policy from a template**

A template is a working, valid, evaluable policy in a shape people actually write — the first twenty clicks of the editor already made. `template` names one (see GET /admin-api/xacml/policies), `name` names the directory entry, and each parameter is sent as `p_<name>`; anything omitted takes the template's own default, so a call with only `template` produces the documented example.

`blank` is the one template that is not an example: it builds an EMPTY Policy, or an empty PolicySet with `p_kind=policyset` — which is the only way to create one of those without ALFA. An empty deny-unless-permit document DENIES rather than answering NotApplicable, so build it before making it the root.

A template BUILDS THE MODEL and the writer serializes it, rather than substituting into XML text — so a role called `a"b` cannot produce a document that will not parse.

The FIRST policy in an empty repository becomes the root, because a repository with a policy and no root decides nothing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Names the DIRECTORY ENTRY. The PolicyId inside the document is a separate identifier and may be any URI. |
| `template` | string | yes | Which template. GET /admin-api/xacml/policies lists them with the parameters each takes. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/decide

`getXacmlDecision`

**Ask the PDP about somebody and see the decision, which policies applied, and what the embedded PEP would do with it**

Everything the Try a decision tab on /admin/xacml draws. `subject`, `action` and `resource` are query parameters; with none of them it answers `asked: false` rather than deciding about nobody.

THE DECISION AND THE ENFORCEMENT ARE TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS and both are here, which is the whole point of the page: the PDP says Permit, Deny, NotApplicable or Indeterminate, and the PEP then applies its bias and the obligation rule to get to allowed or refused. When a policy "is not working" it is nearly always because only one of those was being looked at.

This is NOT POST /xacml/pdp. That endpoint takes a JSON Profile request and is what a PEP calls; this builds a three-category request out of three parameters and is what a person asks.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

## POST /admin-api/xacml/delete

`deleteXacmlPolicy`

**Remove a policy from the repository**

Deleting the ROOT leaves the repository deciding nothing, and the reply says so rather than letting it be discovered by a Deny.

AN APPLICATION'S FINE-GRAINED POLICY (#564) is deleted only when no application names it in appFgaPolicy — an orphan of a deleted application (`applicationPolicies` on GET /admin-api/xacml/policies marks which). ## POST /admin-api/xacml/disable-pep

`disableXacmlPep`

**Stop nudging a registered remote PEP**

IT DOES NOT STOP IT ENFORCING, and the reply says so rather than letting that be discovered. A remote PEP holds its own copy of the engine and its own copy of the policy; nothing in this API reaches into another process. What changes is that this service no longer dials it when the repository changes, so it converges only on its own polling interval.

Named with a `-pep` suffix rather than reusing `disable` because this endpoint dispatches on the action name across the whole family, and a second `disable` would be ambiguous between a policy and a PEP.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

The three attributes of an `AttributeAssignmentExpression`. Its VALUE is the expression underneath it, edited with the set-expression and edit-value actions at the `...assignments.<n>.expression` path.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/edit-variable

`renameXacmlVariable`

**Rename a variable, and every reference with it**

EVERY `VariableReference` NAMING IT IS REWRITTEN. The alternative — refusing to rename one that is used — is safe and useless, since a variable nobody references is the only one nobody wants to rename; and a rename that left the references behind would produce a document that does not load, so the write would be refused and nothing would change. The reply says how many references moved.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/editor

`getXacmlEditor`

**One policy as an editable tree, with what may legally be added at each node**

Everything the Policy editor tab on /admin/xacml draws. `?policy=<name>` chooses one; without it, the root.

Each node in `tree` carries `options.additions` — the elements XACML allows AT THAT POINT, computed against the real function library by the same code that validates the result. That is what makes this usable as an API and not only as a page: a caller can walk the tree, read the legal moves, and POST one, without a second copy of the grammar.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

## POST /admin-api/xacml/import-alfa

`importXacmlAlfa`

**Create a policy from ALFA**

ALFA — the Abbreviated Language For Authorization — is the readable syntax for XACML: forty lines of XML are eight of ALFA. Send it as `alfa` and a name as `name`.

IT IS PARSED, CONVERTED AND STORED AS XACML XML. The repository holds ONE representation, because two would be two documents that could disagree — GET /admin-api/xacml/editor renders the ALFA back from the model whenever you want to read it.

EVERY ATTRIBUTE MUST BE DECLARED BEFORE IT IS USED. That is ALFA's own rule and it is the most useful refusal in the parser: a typo in an attribute name is otherwise a policy that quietly matches nothing, which looks exactly like a policy that is working and denying you.

ALFA IS AN OASIS COMMITTEE SPECIFICATION DRAFT, not a ratified standard — no conformance suite, no schema, no second implementation to disagree with. The contract offered is the one that can be kept: anything this service EMITS as ALFA it reads back, and the policy decides identically either way.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alfa` | string | yes | The ALFA source. Parsed, converted and stored as XACML XML — the repository holds ONE representation. |
| `name` | string | yes | Names the directory entry. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/issue-pep-certificate

`issueXacmlPepCertificate`

**Issue a remote PEP the certificate and private key for its HTTPS listener**

Generates a key pair and certifies it from the Remote PEP listeners (`pep-tls`) Issuing CA of THE REALM THE PEP REGISTERED TO — the realm this call is made in, because ou=peps is per realm — so a client that installed this service's Root CA verifies the PEP, and the chain says which realm vouched for it. A realm whose branch was built before that Issuing CA existed gets it added under its existing Intermediate; nothing already issued is replaced.

The PEP must be REGISTERED: its row is the one record that it exists in this realm. That is not a permission check on the PEP — registering is still not what lets it pull or enforce.

THE CERTIFICATE NAMES the PEP's registered name (where that is a DNS name), the hostname it reported on its registration or heartbeat (#1760; the name its derived notify URL looks for, so the nudge works on a fresh install), and the host of its notify URL, plus any `dnsNames` and `ipAddresses` sent. It certifies `serverAuth` and nothing else.

**THE PRIVATE KEY IS IN THIS REPLY AND NOWHERE ELSE.** This service records the certificate — its issuer's CRL and OCSP responder answer for it — and keeps no copy of the key, so nothing can read it back. To put the pair in the container, write `fullChainPem` (the leaf followed by its Issuing CA, the realm Intermediate and, since #1064, the service Root) and `privateKeyPem` to the files `PEP_HTTPS_CERT` and `PEP_HTTPS_KEY` name; the PEP picks up a pair written after it started. `anchorPem` is the service Root a client of that listener installs.

Issuing again REPLACES: the certificate it replaces goes on its issuer's revocation list as `superseded` (`replacedSerialHex`).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer |  | The lifetime. Defaults to `pki.leafLifetimeDays`, and is shortened to the Issuing CA's own expiry. |
| `dnsNames` | list, or string |  |  |
| `dnsNames[]` | string |  |  |
| `ipAddresses` | list, or string |  |  |
| `ipAddresses[]` | string |  |  |
| `keyAlg` | one of `ec-p256`, `ec-p384`, `ec-p521`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096` |  | The key algorithm. Defaults to `ec-p256`. Only the RSA and NIST-curve ECDSA keys a TLS stack serves are offered. |
| `name` | string |  | The registered PEP's name, as GET /admin-api/xacml/peps lists it. |
| `pep` | string |  | The registered PEP's name under the member GET /admin-api/xacml/peps calls it, ?pep= (2026-11-14). Send `pep` or `name`; both, they must name the same PEP. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

|---|---|---|---|
| `anchorPem` | string |  |  |
| `certificatePem` | string |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/xacml/monitor

`getXacmlMonitor`

**How many authorization decisions are being made, by which enforcement point, and how many are refusals**

Everything /admin/xacml/monitor draws: the global figures — policies, enforcement points, decisions, allows, declines — and then every PEP with its own counts, EMBEDDED and REMOTE in one list.

**A DECISION IS NOT AN ENFORCEMENT.** XACML has four decisions (Permit, Deny, NotApplicable, Indeterminate) and a PEP has two outcomes, and what maps between them is the PEP's BIAS: a deny-biased PEP refuses a NotApplicable that a permit-biased one allows, from the same decision on the same request. An obligation the PEP cannot discharge also turns a Permit into a refusal (section 7.2) — the one enforcement outcome that looks like a bug from the client side and is the specification working. So `allowed` is not `permit`, and both are reported.

**WHAT THIS SERVICE SAW IS NOT WHAT IT WAS TOLD.** `decisions.here` was counted by this process as it happened; `decisions.remote` is what registered PEPs REPORT on their heartbeats, cumulative in their own memory, and a PEP that restarts makes it go down. `decisions.combined` adds the two, which is the figure a deployment wants and is arithmetic over two kinds of evidence rather than a measurement.

**THE EMBEDDED PEPS ARE NOT "REGISTERED" AND CANNOT BE.** They are compiled into this process, so their existence is a fact about the build. A remote PEP registers because it has no other way to be known about — and even that is not a permission: an unregistered PEP can pull GET /xacml/pep/policies and enforce perfectly, and appears here nowhere. This is every enforcement point the service KNOWS ABOUT, which is a smaller claim than every one that exists.

The counters are IN MEMORY, start with the process (`since`) and are per trust realm. The durable record of a refusal is GET /admin-api/audit, which has the reason as well as the count.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml/monitor` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

## GET /admin-api/xacml/peps

`getXacmlPeps`

**The REMOTE Policy Enforcement Points that pull this repository, and whether they are deciding with the same policy this service holds**

Everything the Remote PEPs tab on /admin/xacml draws.

A REMOTE PEP runs in another process, holds its own copy of the engine and PULLS the enabled policies from GET /xacml/pep/policies. The pull is the contract; the nudge this service sends to `notifyUrl` when the repository changes is an optimisation over the polling interval and never a replacement for it, so a PEP that is never nudged still converges.

REGISTERING IS NOT A PERMISSION. An unregistered PEP can pull and enforce exactly as well — GET /xacml/pep/policies requires no credential, because a policy is a rule and a rule nobody can read is a rule nobody can check. What a row buys is this listing and an address for the nudge.

`current` is a COMPARISON this service performs between `syncToken` on the row and the repository's own, not a claim the PEP makes; `stale` is how long since it was last heard from against xacml.pepStaleAfterS and changes nothing this service does. The decision counts are the PEP's own, cumulative in its process — this service saw none of those decisions, which is what a remote PEP is — so a PEP that restarts makes them go down.

With `pep`, the answer is ONE PEP's page (#1760, `/admin/xacml/pep?pep=<name>`): `peps` holds that row alone and `found` says whether it is registered. Every answer carries `settingsCatalogue`: each setting an administrator may set for a remote PEP (its member name, the environment variable it replaces at the PEP, its type, bounds and closed set, its default, when a change takes effect, and whether this realm's mode refuses `true`), the environment variables that stay the PEP's own with why, and the precedence — the service's value, then the environment's, then the default. Each row carries `settings` (what is set here, null for none), `settingsProblem`, `settingsInUse` (what the PEP last reported having in force, by source) and `settingsCurrent` (whether that was applied from what would be sent now), and `effectiveNotifyUrl`, the address the nudge dials.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml, GET /admin/xacml/pep and GET /admin/xacml/pep/route` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| `pep` | query | string |  | One registered PEP, by its name exactly. The answer then lists that row alone and says `found`; a name with no row answers 200 with `found: false`. |
| `route` | query | string |  | With `pep`: one route of that PEP's reverse proxy, by its id. The answer then carries `routeDetail`: the route, where it stands, whether its application resolves and which proxy listeners serve it; `found: false` there when the PEP has no such route. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/xacml/policies

`getXacmlPolicies`

**The policy repository, with the type-check problems of each**

Everything the Policies tab on /admin/xacml draws.

THE STORE IS `ou=policies` IN THE EMBEDDED DIRECTORY — that container IS the repository rather than a copy of one, so an `ldapmodify` of `xacmlPolicyDocument` changes what the PDP decides on the next request.

EXACTLY ONE POLICY IS THE ROOT. A PDP evaluates one document and reaches the rest through PolicyIdReference, so the root is where evaluation starts; a repository with none decides nothing and reports `root: null`.

`templates` is what POST /admin-api/xacml/create-from-template will build, with the parameters each takes.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The policies, the root, and the templates.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

## POST /admin-api/xacml/remove

`removeXacmlNode`

**Remove any node from a policy**

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-designator

`setXacmlDesignator`

**Make an expression an attribute reference**

An `<AttributeDesignator>`: reads an attribute out of the REQUEST, or out of the directory through the PIP when the id is a bare name or carries the `urn:sts:xacml:attribute:` prefix.

**IT RETURNS A BAG**, always, even when it finds exactly one value — which is why `string-one-and-only` exists and why most functions need it wrapped. Nothing in this engine ever holds a bare value, so there is no code path where somebody has to remember to wrap one.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-function

`setXacmlExpressionFunction`

**Replace an expression with a Function reference**

A function named as a VALUE rather than applied: `<Function FunctionId="..."/>`, which is what the first argument of a higher-order function such as `any-of`, `all-of` or `map` takes.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-selector

`setXacmlExpressionSelector`

**Replace an expression with an AttributeSelector**

An XPath over the `<Content>` of a request category, rather than a named attribute — and it returns a BAG exactly as a designator does, so most functions still need a `one-and-only` around it.

The namespace bindings its prefixes need TRAVEL WITH THE DOCUMENT: a prefix in the path means nothing without one, and an unresolvable prefix is an empty bag, which is NotApplicable, which looks exactly like a policy that decided you may not. Set them with edit-selector.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | string |  | The request category whose content the path runs over. Defaults to resource. |
| `path` | string | yes | The node's address, from GET /admin-api/xacml/editor. ONLY VALID AGAINST THE DOCUMENT IT WAS READ FROM: remove rule 0 and every path naming rule 1 now means rule 0. |
| `path_xpath` | string |  | Sent as `path` — but `path` is already the node address on this endpoint, so set the XPath with edit-selector immediately afterwards. The selector arrives with `//*`, which is complete and valid. |
| `policy` | string | yes | The directory entry name of the policy to edit — the `cn` under ou=policies, not the PolicyId inside the document. |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-listener

`setXacmlPepListener`

**Define or replace one of a remote PEP's listeners**

Adds a listener to a registered remote PEP, or replaces the one with its id, beyond the four its environment binds (#1760). The PEP pulls the definitions from GET /xacml/pep/settings and binds a new one, unbinds a removed one and rebinds a changed one while it runs, with no restart; it reports each on its heartbeat (listenerRows on GET /admin-api/xacml/peps). An HTTPS listener's key is generated by the PEP, which asks POST /xacml/pep/listener-certificate for its certificate from the realm's pep-tls Issuing CA, so no private key is in this call or its answer. Validated whole: STS-XACML-0243 (not an object, a stray member, more than 32), 0244 (the id), 0245 (protocol, purpose), 0246 (address, port), 0247 (an address and port another listener holds, the environment's as the PEP last reported them), 0248 (certificate names or key), and in product mode a plain-HTTP proxy listener 0249 unless xacml.pepPlainHttpProxyListeners is on.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-proxy

`setXacmlPepProxy`

**Configure a registered remote PEP as a reverse proxy in front of an application**

Sets the configuration a registered remote PEP pulls from GET /xacml/pep/proxy (#1760) and enforces as a reverse proxy in front of one application: `enabled`, the `upstream` it forwards to (absolute http or https, no user name, query or fragment — fixed per PEP, so no request can choose where it is forwarded), the `publicBaseUrl` a browser reaches the proxy at (an origin; required when a route uses the session mechanism, https in product mode), `upstreamTimeoutMs` (1 to 120000, default 10000), `maxBodyBytes` (0 to 104857600, default 1048576) and the ORDERED `routes`, first match wins, at most 64. A route has a unique `id`, a `path` (starting with /, no . or .. segment, no //, %, backslash, ? or #), `match` (`prefix` at a segment boundary, or `exact`), `methods` (empty for any), `public` (no credential and no XACML decision) or at least one of `mechanisms` `session`, `oauth2`, `saml2` and `basic`, the `application` it fronts (an identifier in this realm's registry; refused on a public route), the XACML `resource` and `action` (empty for the path and the method), how the identity reaches the application, `identity` (`mode` `headers` with up to 16 `headers` of { `name`, `claim` } and a one-character `separator`, `saml` for a signed SAML Response to the application's registered assertion consumer service, or `jwt` for an access token addressed to it; refused on a public route; the proxy strips a client's own identity headers), `forwardCredentials` (false by default: the Authorization header and the proxy's cookie are stripped) and `signals` (true by default: a session route's sign-out reaches the proxy through CAEP/RISC, else through POST /xacml/pep/session).

THE DOCUMENT IS VALIDATED WHOLE AND IS CLOSED: a member the grammar does not name is refused by name, and nothing is written unless all of it is right. What is stored is the document normalised, every member present, which is what the pull sends.

EACH ROUTE NAMES AN APPLICATION AND NOTHING IS COPIED FROM IT: the pull reads what each mechanism needs off the application's entry — the audiences of its access tokens (`oauthAudience`, `oauthPermissionBaseUri`), its SAML entity ID, its confidential OIDC client — so a save is refused, by code, for an unknown application, an oauth2 route whose application has no audience, a saml2 route whose application has no entity ID, and a session route whose application is not a confidential client (client_secret_basic or client_secret_post), does not allow authorization_code, does not register `<publicBaseUrl>/.iya-pep/callback`, or holds no unexpired secret. A session route needs an https publicBaseUrl.

The PEP must be REGISTERED in this realm (its row is where the configuration lives); the proxy picks a change up on its next pull — there is no nudge.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |

| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| `proxy` | map | yes | The configuration document. Validated whole by the handler, which refuses a member it does not name, so this schema leaves its shape to that refusal. |
| `proxy.{key}` | any JSON |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-route

`setXacmlPepRoute`

**Add or replace one route of a remote PEP's reverse proxy**

Adds a route to a registered remote PEP's reverse-proxy configuration, or replaces the one with its id (#1760), and saves the WHOLE document through the same checks as set-pep-proxy — the grammar (STS-XACML-0184 to 0199, 0224 to 0228) and every route's application resolved in the registry (0217 to 0223) — so a route this saves is one the document editor could hold. An edit keeps the route's identity, which set-pep-route-identity sets, unless the form members carry `mode`, as the route's own page sends them; `from` renames the route it names to `id`. The PEP must already hold a configuration (STS-XACML-0201); a missing route or a position outside the list is STS-XACML-0256.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-route-application

`setXacmlPepRouteApplication`

**Map an application to one route of a remote PEP's reverse proxy**

Binds a route of a registered remote PEP's reverse-proxy configuration to an application in this realm's registry (#1760, D10): the route's `application`, from which the pull reads what each mechanism needs. Saved through set-pep-proxy's checks, so an application that does not qualify for the route's mechanisms is refused by its code (STS-XACML-0217 to 0223) and a public route, which names none, by STS-XACML-0197. An unknown route is STS-XACML-0230 and a missing application STS-XACML-0256. Kept for compatibility: the console no longer has a form for it, and edits a route's application on the route's own page (`/admin/xacml/pep/route?pep=<name>&route=<id>`) through set-pep-route.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-route-identity

`setXacmlPepRouteIdentity`

**Set how one reverse-proxy route forwards the identity to its application**

Replaces one route's `identity` in a registered remote PEP's reverse-proxy configuration (#1760, D11) and saves the document through the same checks as set-pep-proxy. `mode` is `headers` (the claims in `headerName` and `headerClaim`, row by row; a row with no name is unused; at most 16; each name an RFC 9110 token that is not hop-by-hop, framing, Authorization, Cookie, Host, Forwarded or X-Forwarded-*, each claim one of sub, username, email, name, given_name, family_name, groups, mechanism, acr and amr; `separator` one printable ASCII character that is not a letter or a digit, `,` by default), `saml` (a signed SAML Response to the application's registered assertion consumer service; its entity ID and ACS are required) or `jwt` (an access token addressed to the application; an audience is required). A public route forwards nobody.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headerClaim` | list |  | Mode headers: the claim each row's header carries, by position. |
| `headerClaim[]` | string |  |  |
| `headerName` | list |  | Mode headers: the header names, one per row of the console's table. |
| `headerName[]` | string |  |  |
| `mode` | one of `headers`, `saml`, `jwt` | yes | How the identity reaches the application. |
| `name` | string |  | The registered PEP's name, as GET /admin-api/xacml/peps lists it. |
| `pep` | string |  | The registered PEP's name under the member GET /admin-api/xacml/peps calls it, ?pep= (2026-11-14). Send `pep` or `name`; both, they must name the same PEP. |
| `route` | string | yes | The route's `id` in that PEP's configuration. |
| `separator` | string |  | Mode headers: the one character a list claim (groups, amr) is joined with. |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-pep-settings

`setXacmlPepSettings`

**Set a remote PEP's managed settings, over its environment**

Sets the settings a registered remote PEP pulls from GET /xacml/pep/settings and applies while it runs (#1760), REPLACING what was set: the settings are sent as `settings`, an object of them, or as members of the body itself (the console's form), and a setting absent, null or empty is NOT SET, so the PEP uses its environment variable for it, or its default — THE PRECEDENCE IS THE SERVICE'S VALUE, THEN THE ENVIRONMENT'S, THEN THE DEFAULT. GET /admin-api/xacml/peps' `settingsCatalogue` lists every setting with its variable, type, bounds, default and when a change takes effect. Validated whole: a member of `settings` that is not a setting is refused by name (STS-XACML-0236), a wrong type or a value outside a closed set (bias, logLevel) STS-XACML-0237, an integer out of bounds STS-XACML-0238, text too long or with a control character, a notifyUrl that is not an absolute http(s) URL and an authzenPdpIdentifier that is not an https origin STS-XACML-0239, and in product mode proxyUpstreamInsecure or proxyRpAllowInsecure true STS-XACML-0240. THE MINIMUM THE PEP NEEDS TO CONNECT THE FIRST TIME IS NOT HERE AND CANNOT BE: the service's URL, the PEP's name, its client certificate, key and anchors, the ports it binds and the files its TLS stacks read stay in its environment (`settingsCatalogue.bootstrap`). The PEP must be registered in this realm; it applies a change on its next pull — there is no nudge — and an older PEP, which never asks, goes on using its environment.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `authzen` | boolean |  | Sets `authzen` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `authzenForwardTimeoutMs` | integer |  | Sets `authzenForwardTimeoutMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `authzenPdpIdentifier` | string |  | Sets `authzenPdpIdentifier` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `backoffMaxMs` | integer |  | Sets `backoffMaxMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `bias` | one of `deny-biased`, `permit-biased` |  | Sets `bias` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `description` | string |  | Sets `description` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `heartbeatIntervalMs` | integer |  | Sets `heartbeatIntervalMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `httpsReloadIntervalMs` | integer |  | Sets `httpsReloadIntervalMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `logLevel` | one of `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal` |  | Sets `logLevel` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `maxBodyBytes` | integer |  | Sets `maxBodyBytes` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `name` | string |  | The registered PEP's name, as GET /admin-api/xacml/peps lists it. |
| `notifyUrl` | string |  | Sets `notifyUrl` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `pep` | string |  | The registered PEP's name under the member GET /admin-api/xacml/peps calls it, ?pep= (2026-11-14). Send `pep` or `name`; both, they must name the same PEP. |
| `pip` | boolean |  | Sets `pip` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |

| `proxyJwksTtlMs` | integer |  | Sets `proxyJwksTtlMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |

| `proxyMaxSessions` | integer |  | Sets `proxyMaxSessions` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `proxyRpAllowInsecure` | boolean |  | Sets `proxyRpAllowInsecure` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `proxySessionRecheckMs` | integer |  | Sets `proxySessionRecheckMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `proxySessionTtlMs` | integer |  | Sets `proxySessionTtlMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |

| `proxySignalsStaleMs` | integer |  | Sets `proxySignalsStaleMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `proxyStripCookies` | string |  | Sets `proxyStripCookies` at the PEP: more cookie names the reverse proxy never forwards upstream, beside this service's own, separated by commas, a trailing `*` a prefix; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses PEP_PROXY_STRIP_COOKIES or its default, none. |
| `proxyUpstreamInsecure` | boolean |  | Sets `proxyUpstreamInsecure` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `resource` | string |  | Sets `resource` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |
| `settings` | map |  | The settings as one object, in place of the members below. Validated whole by the handler, which refuses a member that is not a setting by name. |
| `settings.{key}` | any JSON |  |  |
| `timeoutMs` | integer |  | Sets `timeoutMs` at the PEP; absent, null or empty is not set, so the PEP uses its environment variable or its default. |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-root

`setXacmlRootPolicy`

**Choose the policy the PDP starts from**

Clears the flag on the incumbent first, because the store refuses a second root. Done in that order deliberately: a failure then leaves the repository with NO root rather than with two, which is the recoverable one of the two bad states.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The policy's directory entry name. |
